findings.title: Progress/lifetime over-counting (three P0 data-corruption escapes) got through because fixtures used globally-unique IDs — no collision or property-based fixtures exist
findings.evidence: Three separate P0 data-integrity escapes in the scope-id keying: (1) e22fb126 — level3/4 lifetime marks stored BARE unitIdentifier, so marking daf '2' in Berakhos credited daf 2 in EVERY masechta ('1.3% after one daf' symptom); (2) bf92cde9 — the v30 fix left level2 BARE assuming masechta-uniqueness, but perek '1' exists in all five chumashim, so marking Bereishis perek 1 cross-credited +170 pesukim across every sefer; (3) 98d5e64b — the Tanach over-count 'passed CI but FAILED on-device — the v32 migration ran but the ledger row survived the per-account DB and aggregation still honored it at read time,' inflating the headline total from correct ~1542 to ~5852. findings.impact: Children's lifetime learning totals and completion percentages were silently inflated (siyum milestones, rewards, streaks all key off these). Corrupts the core value metric of the app and can wrongly trigger reward unlocks.

Add a property test: sum of per-leaf credits == number of distinctly-marked leaves. Assert migrations at READ time (drop-then-aggregate), not just that the migration statement ran — 98d5e64b proves a green migration test does not prove read-time correctness.

findings.title: 63 provider-staleness escapes: there is no systemic 'provider re-executes on its invalidation tick' harness — reactivity is tested reactively, one bug at a time, after each stale-UI report
findings.evidence: 63 fix commits match stale|reactiv|sentinel|cold-start|invalidate. Same defect shape repeats across every feature: a Riverpod provider computes a derived view but never ref.watch-es the mutation tick, so the UI shows stale data until pull-to-refresh. Examples: d5b53992 (itemsLearned/lifetimeView/curriculumProgress never watched completionCommittedProvider), 0699e9b9, 16e54ec4, 084f254f, c9858974, a0dc2a73, 237fd876 (gamification balances/redemptions/achievements stale after mutation), fc9073a6 (goal stale after EditTrack), 66a3e0b0 (sync badge stuck). Each ships its own bespoke 're-executes on tick' regression test only after the escape — proof no general contract existed. Widget/unit tests asserted a single post-build snapshot, so the missing subscription was undetectable.
findings.impact: Stale points/balances/progress/achievements shown to child and parent after every completion, redemption, or edit — reported repeatedly as bugs over 3 months. A wrong reward balance is a trust/data-integrity issue.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a reusable reactivity contract test: for each derived provider, mutate its upstream source (or bump the tick provider) inside a ProviderContainer and assert the provider re-emits. Enumerate derived providers via a registry so new ones are forced to opt in. This converts 63 reactive one-offs into one enforced invariant.

findings.title: Parent-PIN (P0 auth surface) suffered repeated async nav-guard/lifecycle regressions that widget tests structurally cannot reproduce — real AutoRoute completer + keepAlive microtask timing
findings.evidence: At least four PIN-flow escapes in the same controller: b8464ccc (first-time setup loops forever — maybePop didn't complete the push RESULT completer, guard await never returned; 'Root-caused empirically via on-device logcat; static analysis could not pin it down'), a0c85409 (Set-PIN freezes at 4 dots — keepAlive controller default mode=verify, first digits routed to _handleVerify before the reset microtask drained), 24acaf78 (setup didn't call pinGuard.markAuthenticated → guard re-push infinite loop), plus acaa2660/56a6ff50 keepAlive stale-digit races. The passing tests exercised the verify DIALOG path; the real bug lived in the router-push-result and AutoRoute guard re-evaluation timing, a seam the widget harness resolves differently than a device.
findings.impact: Users trapped at 'Set Parent PIN' (PIN saved but inaccessible until force-restart) — a hard lockout of the parental-control gate, the app's auth boundary. Repeatedly regressed.
findings.proposed_fix: Add integration_test/ coverage that drives the real AutoRoute guard + PinFlowSetupRoute push-and-await on a device/emulator, asserting the guard resolver.next fires and Parent hub opens. For the keepAlive race, add a test that dispatches digit gestures synchronously before any microtask drains. These races are unreachable from pumpWidget alone.

findings.title: Parent-PIN escalation guard test stubs the guard DECISION and re-implements its logic inside the test — a tautology that cannot catch a real guard regression
findings.evidence: AN-2 guards edit/delete/add-profile/switch-account on a CHILD profile behind a Parent PIN (P0 child-privacy path). The widget tests override switcherSheetPinGuardRequiredProvider.overrideWith((ref) async => pinGuardRequired) (line ~72) — the real decision (active profile is child AND a PIN is configured in FlutterSecureStorage) is replaced by a hardcoded bool. The 'unit' test (line ~230) overrides the SAME provider with a hand-copied re-implementation of the production logic and asserts that copy returns false — it can never fail from a production bug. Actions are fired via btn.onPressed?.call() (lines ~130,~180), bypassing tester.tap/hit-testing ('to avoid InkSparkle shader'). The tests assert find.text('Enter Parent PIN') appears but never enter a PIN, never verify the escalating action is actually BLOCKED, and never test the wrong-PIN path.
findings.impact: A regression where the guard fails to engage for a real child+PIN state (wrong profile-mode check, storage read returning stale true/false) ships green: the decision logic is never exercised, the dialog-shown assertion doesn't prove the action was blocked, and the 'unit' test validates a copy of the code. Mitigated only because pin_service_extended_test.dart covers the hash/lockout primitives.
findings.proposed_fix: Drive the guard through the real switcherSheetPinGuardRequiredProvider with a fake secure-storage seam (child profile + set/unset PIN); use tester.tap; assert the destructive callback does NOT run until a correct PIN is entered, and that a wrong PIN keeps it blocked.

findings.title: Two divergent remoteIsNewer implementations with OPPOSITE tie-break semantics; no test pins the tie behaviour of the merge_rules variant, and study_day_config_merger is its lone user
findings.evidence: merge_rules.dart top-level `remoteIsNewer` returns `remoteUpdatedAt.isAfter(localUpdatedAt)` -> ties go to LOCAL (lib/core/sync/merge/merge_rules.dart:66-73, comment 'ties go to local'). DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer -> ties go to REMOTE (asserted by lww_symmetric_test.dart:1228 'exactly identical timestamps -> remote wins -> isTrue'). Grep shows every merger uses `_store.remoteIsNewer` (tie->remote) EXCEPT study_day_config_merger.dart:78 which calls the bare `remoteIsNewer` (tie->local). LWW convergence between two devices REQUIRES a deterministic, side-independent tie-break; tie->local is non-convergent (both devices keep their own value on equal timestamps -> permanent divergence). No test in test/sync or test/sync/merge exercises study_day_config's equal-timestamp path, and study_day_config_roundtrip_test does not cover it. AUD-docs-08 already flags that the docs' LWW tie-break rule contradicts the implementation; the code-level divergence + test gap compounds it.
findings.impact: study_day_config (which days a child studies) can permanently diverge across a parent's and child's device on an equal-updated_at conflict, with no failing test and a stale schedule that silently never reconciles.
findings.proposed_fix: Collapse to one remoteIsNewer implementation (prefer the store's tie->remote convergent rule) and add an equal-timestamp convergence test to study_day_config_roundtrip_test / lww_symmetric_test covering the study_day_config merger.
findings.verifier_notes:
All factual claims verified against source. merge_rules.dart:72 bare remoteIsNewer uses isAfter -> ties to LOCAL (doc comment 'ties go to local', lines 63-65). DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer (drift_merge_store.dart:151) returns true on equal-updated_at/no-server-ts tie -> ties to REMOTE (explicit convergence comment). study_day_config_merger.dart:78 calls the bare free function; grep confirms every other merger uses _store.remoteIsNewer, and the epic_25_story_13 acceptance test's lwwMergers enforcement list (lines 220-226) enumerates 5 mergers and omits study_day_config, so nothing forces it onto the store rule. Test gap confirmed: study_day_config_roundtrip_test only covers newer/older cases; study_day_config_sync_test covers 'newer overwrites'/'older ignored' -- neither builds local.updatedAt == remote.updatedAt with differing values. Extra corroboration: the bare function has NO clock-skew window, so study_day_config also skips the +/-5s synced_at tie-break every other channel uses.

Caveats. (1) DUPLICATION: TEA-027 heavily overlaps standards finding AUD-core-sync-03 (P1) -- 'Fix StudyDayConfigMerger to use DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer instead of pre-Phase-3 merge_rules.remoteIsNewer' -- the code-fix sibling of the identical defect at the same call site. Recommend it be linked to AUD-core-sync-03 and severity coordinated; if sync-03's code fix lands, the 'opposite semantics' framing dissolves but the test is still worth adding. (2) The 'tie->remote converges / tie->local diverges' argument is only loosely correct -- naive tie->remote also swaps values under truly simultaneous bidirectional pulls; true convergence needs value/device-id ordering. But the codebase's intended house rule is tie->remote (asserted by lww_symmetric_test:1228), so study_day_config deviating from it with zero tie-path test is a real verified inconsistency. findings.title: 953 uses of pump(const Duration(seconds:1)) as a pumpAndSettle substitute — arbitrary fixed waits that mask async races and frame-count dependence
findings.evidence: grep across test/features: 953 occurrences of 'pump(const Duration(seconds: 1))', 267 bare 'pumpAndSettle()', 0 pumpAndSettle-with-timeout. The 1s pump is used as the settle mechanism after provider resolution throughout (tutor_pin_entry_gate_l1_test.dart:225 'await tester.pump(const Duration(seconds: 1));' after a throwing provider; dashboard_screen_test.dart:70; learning_screen_test.dart:47). A fixed 1s clock-advance pumps a bounded number of frames; if an async chain needs an extra microtask/frame or >1s simulated time the assertion runs against a half-settled tree. The pattern is chosen to dodge pumpAndSettle timing out on CircularProgressIndicator/shimmer, trading a timeout for a silent race.
findings.impact: Order/timing-dependent assertions can flip between environments and refactors without a code bug (the '931 fix commits while green' churn signature), and genuinely-async error/empty transitions can be asserted before they occur, hiding real regressions.
findings.proposed_fix: Prefer pump-until-condition helpers or bounded pumpAndSettle; where infinite animations block settle, stub the animation/loading provider to a terminal state rather than guessing a duration.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: 953 occurrences of pump(const Duration(seconds: 1)) across 74 files in test/features; anchor tutor_pin_entry_gate_l1_test.dart:224 confirmed exactly (pump() then pump(1s) after a throwing async provider override, then error-text assertion). 267 bare pumpAndSettle(), 0 pumpAndSettle-with-timeout — confirmed. Referenced dashboard/learning files exist. No duplicate in findings.json (searched pump/settle/Duration; other hits are unrelated production timers and list-virtualization findings). CORRECTNESS: factual claims accurate; the descriptive characterization holds. Caveat: pump(fixedDuration) is the correct Flutter idiom when an indefinite spinner/shimmer would make pumpAndSettle time out, and 1 simulated second advances ~60 frames, so the "silent race/half-settled tree" language and the "931 green-fix churn" attribution are somewhat overstated/speculative — but that does not refute the core observation. MATERIALITY: a 953-instance systemic reliance on an arbitrary magic 1s wait as the universal settle mechanism, combined with zero bounded pumpAndSettle anywhere, is a real, pervasive test-architecture smell squarely within this audit's scope; P2 is reasonable. Finding survives; severity rhetoric slightly inflated but severity level itself correct.

findings.title: 332 bare pumpAndSettle() calls, zero explicit bounded-timeout overrides anywhere in the suite
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'pumpAndSettle()' test/ --include=*.dart | wc -l => 332 (of 350 total pumpAndSettle( calls). grep -rn 'pumpAndSettle(const Duration\|pumpAndSettle(Duration' => 18, none of which specify a shorter fail-fast timeout bound. findings.impact: Bare pumpAndSettle() pumps frames every 100ms until no frame is scheduled, and hangs/times out if any widget under test has a continuous animation (shimmer/loading spinner/lottie) — one of the most common real-world Flutter test flake sources. findings.title: `make ci` silently omits format-check, contradicting learning_tracker/CLAUDE.md's documented pre-commit workflow
findings.evidence: learning_tracker/Makefile:214 `ci: analyze validate-calendar lint-rules-test test` has no `format`/`format-check` prerequisite, yet learning_tracker/CLAUDE.md's documented workflow says step 4 is `make ci` (analyze + format + all stories) before committing, and the CLAUDE.md quick-reference table lists `make ci` as 'analyze + format + all stories'. `format-check` exists as its own target (Makefile:263-264, `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .`) but nothing wires it into `ci`. hooks/pre-commit does run dart format, but hooks/README.md requires a manual `cp hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/` step and `.git/hooks/` on this checkout has no hook installed.
findings.impact: Developers who follow the project's own documented workflow get a false local all-clear on formatting; the only backstop is the separate `format-check` GitHub Actions job, meaning formatting violations are only ever caught remotely, wasting a full CI round-trip on a class of failure the local command was supposed to prevent.

findings.title: Process-wide mutable caches guarded only by debug reset hooks leak state across tests
findings.evidence: `bool _lastKnownOnline = false;` (connectivity_providers.dart:36) is a process-wide mutable connectivity cache read by connectivity-aware screens' loading state; it is NOT reset by a `connectivityStreamProvider` override (the file's own doc-comment warns of this) and is cleared only if a test calls `debugResetLastKnownOnline()` / seeds via `debugSetLastKnownOnline(true)`. Combined with `currentLocalDayClock` (previous finding), the codebase relies on 17 `@visibleForTesting`/`debugReset`/`debugSet` hooks (grep) to scrub globals between tests. Any test that forgets a reset inherits a leaked value — for connectivity this means a screen renders the online 'your data is backed up' card in a test that intended offline, passing for the wrong reason.
findings.impact: Cross-test state bleed is a direct contributor to a green suite that fails to catch regressions: outcomes depend on isolate execution order and on every author remembering manual reset calls, not on isolated construction.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the last-known-online seed into provider state (e.g. a `StateProvider`/`Notifier`) scoped per `ProviderContainer` so each test gets a fresh instance with no global to reset; same treatment for the clock. Eliminate the debug reset/set hooks once the state is container-scoped.

Correctness holds on every load-bearing claim. `_lastKnownOnline` is a module-level process-wide mutable global (line 34; finding cites 36 — trivial doc-comment offset, immaterial) read by sign_in_screen.dart:260 and signup_screen.dart:514 via `orElse: () => lastKnownOnline`. A connectivityStreamProvider override genuinely does NOT reset it — it lives outside the ProviderContainer, and the file's own doc-comment (lines 48-52) explicitly warns of this trap. Reset only via debugResetLastKnownOnline/debugSetLastKnownOnline. The "17 hooks" grep count is confirmed exactly. Mechanism (cross-test state bleed within an isolate) is real.

NOT a duplicate: AUD-core-time-01 (the "previous finding" TEA-040 references) targets a different global, currentLocalDayClock in core/time; AUD-t-auth-02 mentions debugResetLastKnownOnline only incidentally and is substantively a registry-mode coverage-gap finding. TEA-040 addresses a distinct global worth its own fix.

Severity correction: this is latent, not demonstrated — every observed test correctly pairs a tearDown/reset (auth_p0/p1, onboarding, signup, sign_in tests). The materially identical sibling AUD-core-time-01, with the same "no compiler-enforced pairing / convention-enforced risk rather than demonstrated failure" reasoning, is rated P3. findings.title: Seven DAOs bake DateTimeFactory.now/DateTime.now() into production code with no injectable clock, forcing their tests into isNotNull-only assertions on the very timestamps the DAO writes
findings.evidence: Code-under-test calls wall-clock now() with no seam in lib/core/database/daos/: outbox_dao.dart, track_dao.dart, text_download_status_dao.dart, active_curriculum_dao.dart, study_day_config_dao.dart, curriculum_scope_dao.dart, points_balance_dao.dart. Consequence in tests: track_dao_test.dart resetPace asserts only `row!.paceResetDate, isNotNull` (test/core/database/daos/track_dao_test.dart ~line 297-303) rather than the actual written value, because the value is a non-deterministic wall-clock read. This is distinct from the register's DateTime.now findings (AUD-t-cross-83/85 etc.), which target test-file fixtures; here the missing seam is in production DAO code and it is what weakens the assertion.
findings.impact: DAO methods that stamp created/updated/reset timestamps (the fields LWW sync and progress ordering depend on) can only be asserted for presence, not correctness; a DAO writing the wrong clock field, wrong timezone, or a stale/zero value passes.
findings.proposed_fix: Inject a Clock/DateTimeFactory seam into these DAOs (or pass timestamps in from the caller) so tests can assert the exact written value; then tighten resetPace-style assertions from isNotNull to equality against the injected instant.

findings.title: core/ids sync-dedup natural-key factories at 10% with no test/core/ids directory
findings.evidence: lib/core/ids = 2/20 LH = 10.0%; natural_key.dart's per-entity factory constructors encode the dedup identity ('the set of columns that uniquely identifies a row', replacing ad-hoc '$a|$b' concatenations) used by 6 merger files. There is no test/core/ids/ directory (confirmed MISSING). The factories are exercised only transitively through mergers, so a wrong key-shape for one entity has no direct guard.
findings.impact: An incorrect natural-key factory silently breaks dedup for one entity type → duplicate or wrongly-merged synced rows; covered only indirectly.
findings.proposed_fix: Add test/core/ids/natural_key_test.dart asserting the exact key string each factory produces for representative inputs.

findings.title: Near-zero coverage on PIN, tutor-audit and scheduler domain files is dead duplicate risk-logic — the live paths lack a canonical tested domain layer
findings.evidence: Several risk-labelled files show ~0% coverage because they are DEAD, and the register already flags them: pin_flow_machine.dart PinFlowMachine (addDigit/backspace/transitionAfterAsync/setup-confirm logic) is 1/88 LH — `grep -rn 'PinFlowMachine(' lib` returns nothing; the live pin_flow_controller.dart (84/96 covered) reimplements backspace()/_onFourDigits()/_initialStep() as a parallel copy (AUD-profiles-06/07). set_parent_pin_use_case.dart & verify_parent_pin_use_case.dart are 0% and referenced nowhere outside their own files. tutor_audit_log_writer.dart (the child-data mutation audit trail, FR-7.2) is 0/33 and constructed nowhere (AUD-tutoring-06). The coverage-lens insight beyond the register: the intended single testable 'pure domain' PIN machine is the DEAD copy, so the LIVE PIN entry/confirm/lockout logic exists only inside a StateNotifier and every future PIN fix must be re-proven against the widget-level path, not a unit-testable machine.
findings.impact: PIN entry/confirm/lockout and tutor-audit accountability logic have no canonical unit-tested home; the 0% readings also inflate the risk-file list and hide that live coverage is thinner than it looks.

findings.title: Two dead, 100%-skipped placeholder test files with no real test bodies
findings.evidence: test/sync/sync_rework_engine_test.dart: 5 groups, all skip:'Retired W2.35 — ...', each containing only test('placeholder', () {}). test/migration/v18_to_v19_test.dart: 1 group skip:'sync_queue table removed in Wave 3 schema rebuild' containing 4 empty test() bodies. Confirmed via file read — every test body in both files is () {} (no assertions, unreachable due to skip).

findings.title: No retry/quarantine infrastructure exists to contain acknowledged flaky tests
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'retry(\|@Retry\|quarantine\|flaky' test/ tool/ finds zero test-infra hits (only unrelated production retry() method names and comments describing PAST flakiness that was fixed by removing fixed delays, e.g. test/core/analytics/streak_milestone_analytics_observer_test.dart:128 and :165, test/features/account/presentation/providers/connectivity_providers_test.dart:323).
findings.impact: When a genuinely flaky test appears (the codebase's own comments show it has happened before), the only available responses are: fix it properly, delete it, or skip: true (which per the prior finding silently drops coverage with no tracking). There is no tagged-quarantine lane that keeps a flaky test running-but-non-blocking while someone investigates.

findings.title: 41% of test files (320/780) exceed 300 lines; several exceed 1,600-3,600 lines
findings.evidence: find test/ -name '*.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>300' | wc -l => 320. Ten largest: test/story_acceptance/epic_15_multi_profile_test.dart (3588 lines), test/core/database/user_database_managers_orderby_test.dart (2435), test/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl_test.dart (2039), test/story_acceptance/epic_25_schema_core_test.dart (2036), test/core/sync/merge/drift_merge_store_test.dart (1842), test/core/sync/outbox/outbox_processor_test.dart (1773).
findings.impact: Very large test files correlate with the observed pattern of many independent magic-delay pumps and skip clauses accreting undetected inside them (e.g. drift_merge_store_test.dart alone contributes 10 of the skip-annotated test cases at lines 814-1694) — reviewers cannot realistically hold a 3,588-line or 2,435-line test file's invariants in their head during a fix-commit review, plausibly contributing to the observed 931 fix/bug commits landing without the suite catching regressions in adjacent, unreviewed assertions within the same giant file.

findings.title: Skip-if-absent soft-gate pattern is duplicated identically across 3 separate ci.yml jobs with no single point of control
findings.evidence: The same `if [ -f <marker file/target> ]; then run; else echo ::notice ...skipping; fi` idiom appears independently in the `audit` job (line ~130, guarded by `make -n audit`), the `firestore-rules` job (line ~354, guarded by existence of functions/test/firestore_rules.test.mjs), and the `arb-parity` job (line ~420, guarded by existence of tool/arb_parity_check.dart). TQ-9 already documents the firestore-rules instance as a soft-skip risk.
findings.impact: Each of these three checks can be silently un-gated by an accidental deletion/rename of its target file/tool during a bad merge or revert, and because the pattern is copy-pasted three times rather than centralized, a fix applied to one (e.g. converting firestore-rules to hard-fail per TQ-9's recommendation) leaves the other two exposed to the identical failure mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the three ad-hoc existence checks with one convention (e.g. a required-files manifest checked once in a leading job, hard-failing the whole workflow if any expected gate artifact is missing) so 'the file disappeared' is always a hard CI failure, never a silent skip.
